new_statements.translation: The Higashi-ku dialect of Yoron Island is not an N-pattern accent (e.g. a three-pattern one) as earlier studies claimed, but a 'multi-pattern accent system with Pn = n+1', distinguished by an 'ascending kernel'. A multi-pattern accent system based on an ascending kernel was previously unknown among the Ryukyuan dialects. [...] This dialect is characterised by its word-final kernel: [1] the accent system is mora-based, but a moraic phoneme can bear the kernel only in absolute word-final position; [2] the word-final kernel shows an alternation whereby, when (i) another phrase follows without a particle or (ii) a particle of two or more moras is attached, the kernel shifts to the initial mora of that phrase or particle. (p. 188) [§3.2, p. 183:] From (8) one sees that an n-mora word has n+1 distinctions, the patterns being distinguished from one another by the position of the pitch rise; that is, this is a dialect with an 'ascending kernel' /「/ ...

new_statements.rule_in_words: Lexical pitch accent, not stress. Each accent unit has at most one 'ascending kernel' (the mora at which pitch rises); for an n-mora noun there are n+1 contrastive patterns: unaccented (spoken at mid pitch) or the kernel on any one of the n moras (Uwano labels positions from the word end: -1 final, -2 penultimate, -3.; e.g. Higashi-ku pa:= 'leaf' unaccented, pa[: 'tooth' final kernel, [pa: 'outside' initial kernel; ja[ma 'mountain', [nabi 'pot'; ha[tana, [macjigi; puru[sjiki, hu[baNka, [karatai). The kernel position is lexically given, not predictable from word shape. Moraic phonemes (second half of a long vowel, N, diphthong offglide) can carry the kernel only in absolute word-final position; a word-final kernel moves onto the first mora of a following particle of two or more moras (jama[kara) or of a following phrase, while a one-mora particle leaves it in place (ja[manu). Compounds are mostly -2 type (Uwano 2016 NB38, 2018).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not applicable / not mentioned: one kernel per accent unit; no secondary prominence is described. Uwano notes that the pitch range is small, 'delayed rise' and 'delayed fall' are frequent, and utterance-final (言い切り) forms carry a phrase-final fall that is not part of the lexical contrast.
new_statements.exceptions: (a) Moraic phonemes bear the kernel only in absolute final position; with anything following, the kernel shifts one mora right (pa[: 'tooth' ~ pa:[nu). (b) Final-kernel words shift the kernel onto a following >=2-mora particle or following phrase. (c) Long words: the initial-kernel (-n / type 1) pattern is hard to find for 6+ moras. (d) Dialect variation on the island (Uwano 2016 NINJAL pp. 25-27; Uwano 2018): the 'intermediate' villages Asato, Kanō, Nama, Ritchō, Gusuku merge the final-kernel type with the unaccented type in isolation and with 1-mora particles, giving Pn = n (Kanō explicitly Pn = n); Chabana is furthest reduced. (e) Earlier descriptions (Hirayama et al. 1966, Sakimura 1986, Nakamoto & Shinozaki 1989) analysed Higashi-ku as a 2-3 pattern N-type system; Uwano 1999 refutes this.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the accent unit = word (noun) alone or noun + particle (bunsetsu); Uwano distinguishes the utterance-final 'citation/final form' (言い切り形, with a non-distinctive final fall) from the 'connective form' (接続形). Nouns of 2-7 moras in Higashi-ku; verbs treated separately. Description is mora-based.
new_statements.identity_note: The deciding description is of the Mugiya-Higashi-ku (麦屋東区) dialect of Yoron Island, the most conservative variety (Pn = n+1); Uwano 2016 (NINJAL report, pp. 25-27) and Uwano 2018 show the other villages (Asato, Kanō, Nama, Ritchō, Gusuku; Chabana) have reduced Pn = n systems with the same ascending-kernel type. All fall under Glottolog yoro1243 (no dialect-level glottocodes). The Glottolog ref 663799 'Okinoerabu hōgen chōsa hōkoku-sho' is the same NINJAL 2016 volume that contains the Yoron chapters (full title Yoron hōgen, Okinoerabu hōgen chōsa hōkokusho).

sources.note: Primary description. Higashi-ku (Mugiya-Higashi) Yoron has a mora-based multi-pattern pitch accent system (Pn = n+1 for n-mora nouns) distinguished by an 'ascending kernel' (position where pitch rises), not an N-pattern system as earlier work claimed; moraic phonemes bear the kernel only in absolute word-final position; a word-final kernel shifts to the first mora of a following >=2-mora particle or following phrase (pp. 188, 184-183, 181-180).
